name: probable-prime test by a modular-exponentiation witness
mechanism: pick a random base and check an identity that every prime satisfies for that base (base to the modulus minus one is one; the strong form also inspects the sequence of successive square roots); a failure proves compositeness, a pass with many bases makes primality overwhelmingly likely
